'''James Garson''' is an American [[philosopher]] and [[logician]]. He has made significant contributions in the study of [[modal logic]]<ref>{{Cite book|chapter-url=http://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-modal/|title = [[The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy]]|chapter = Modal Logic|year = 2021|publisher = Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University}}</ref> and [[Formal semantics (logic)|formal semantics]]. He is author of ''Modal Logic for Philosophers''<ref name="humberstone">{{cite journal | last= Humberstone | first=Lloyd | title=Reviewed Work: Modal Logic for Philosophers. Second Edition James W. Garson | journal=Studia Logica| publisher=Springer | volume=104 | issue=2 | year=2016 | issn=0039-3215 | jstor=24754808 | pages=365–379 | doi=10.1007/s11225-016-9666-z | url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/24754808 | access-date=2025-01-11}}</ref> and ''What Logics Mean'' by [[Cambridge University Press]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.cambridge.org/gb/knowledge/isbn/item1163165/?site_locale=en_GB| title = Modal logic philosophers 2nd edition {{!}} Logic {{!}} Cambridge University Press}}</ref> Garson is Professor of Philosophy at the [[University of Houston]] and has taught at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], the [[University of Notre Dame]], the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] (where he was a visiting professor in [[computer science]]), and [[Rice University]]. He is a nominalist<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.class.uh.edu/phil/garson/vita.htm |title=Vita |access-date=2011-01-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100807143846/http://www.class.uh.edu/phil/garson/vita.htm |archive-date=2010-08-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
